result:
`./compile.sh` reports success and produced `JsonReaderAgentTest.class` (plus its `FlagCloseReader` fixture) at `tests/com/google/gson/stream/JsonReaderAgentTest.java`.

Summary of coverage (44 `@Test` methods, JUnit 4 style since `junit-4.12.jar` is present in `lib/`):
- `isLenient`/`setLenient` defaults and toggling
- `beginArray`/`endArray`/`beginObject`/`endObject` happy paths and structural mismatches (documented `IOException`)
- `hasNext` transitions in arrays and objects
- `peek` non-consuming behavior across token types (`BEGIN_OBJECT`, `NAME`, `NUMBER`, `END_OBJECT`, `BOOLEAN`, `NULL`)
- `nextName`, `nextString`, `nextBoolean`, `nextNull` happy paths plus their documented `IllegalStateException`/`IOException` cases, including post-`close()` state
- `nextDouble`/`nextLong`/`nextInt`: exact values, string-to-number coercion, `NumberFormatException` for out-of-range/non-finite values, `IllegalStateException` for structural tokens
- `close()` verified to propagate to the underlying `Reader` via a custom fixture
- `skipValue()` for both primitives and recursive nested structures
- `getPath()` root value and change-on-navigation
- `toString()` non-null per `Object` contract
- All documented lenient-mode behaviors: non-execute prefix, multiple top-level values, scalar top-level values, unquoted names/alternate separators, single-quoted strings, `;` array separator, omitted-element nulls — each paired with the corresponding strict-mode rejection where applicable
- Boundary cases: empty stream and truncated/malformed input

I did not test the package-private members (`peeked` field, `doPeek()`, `getLineNumber()`, `getColumnNumber()`) since the javadoc gives no documented contract for them, and asserting on them would mean guessing implementation behavior rather than the spec.
